[189](https://docs.rs#189)
[190](https://docs.rs#190)#[cfg(feature = "iter")]
[191](https://docs.rs#191)impl<'a> Context for IterContext<'a> {
[192](https://docs.rs#192)    fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Option<Formattable> {
[193](https://docs.rs#193)        if key.is_empty() {
[194](https://docs.rs#194)            Some(self.inner)
[195](https://docs.rs#195)        } else {
[196](https://docs.rs#196)            self.outer.get(key)
[197](https://docs.rs#197)        }
[198](https://docs.rs#198)    }
[199](https://docs.rs#199)}
[200](https://docs.rs#200)
[201](https://docs.rs#201)/// Runtime version of [`write!`].
[202](https://docs.rs#202)///
[203](https://docs.rs#203)/// Takes a mutable [`Write`] e.g. `&mut String`, a format string and a context,
[204](https://docs.rs#204)/// containing [`Formattable`] values.
[205](https://docs.rs#205)///
[206](https://docs.rs#206)/// ```
[207](https://docs.rs#207)/// # use std::collections::HashMap;
[208](https://docs.rs#208)/// use interpolator::{write, Formattable};
[209](https://docs.rs#209)///
[210](https://docs.rs#210)/// let mut buf = String::new();
[211](https://docs.rs#211)/// write(
[212](https://docs.rs#212)///     &mut buf,
[213](https://docs.rs#213)///     "{value:+05}", // could be dynamic
[214](https://docs.rs#214)///     &[("value", Formattable::display(&12))]
[215](https://docs.rs#215)///         .into_iter()
[216](https://docs.rs#216)///         .collect::<HashMap<_, _>>(),
[217](https://docs.rs#217)/// )
[218](https://docs.rs#218)/// .unwrap();
[219](https://docs.rs#219)///
[220](https://docs.rs#220)/// assert_eq!(buf, format!("{:+05}", 12));
[221](https://docs.rs#221)/// ```
[222](https://docs.rs#222)///
[223](https://docs.rs#223)/// # Errors
[224](https://docs.rs#224)///
[225](https://docs.rs#225)/// It will return an error if the specified format string has invalid syntax,
[226](https://docs.rs#226)/// the type doesn't implement the expected trait, or the formatting itself
[227](https://docs.rs#227)/// failed.
[228](https://docs.rs#228)///
[229](https://docs.rs#229)/// For more details have a look at [`Error`] and [`ParseError`].
[230](https://docs.rs#230)pub fn write(out: &mut impl Write, mut format: &str, context: &impl Context) -> Result {
[231](https://docs.rs#231)    let format = &mut format;
[232](https://docs.rs#232)    let idx = &mut 0;
[233](https://docs.rs#233)    while !format.is_empty() {
[234](https://docs.rs#234)        if format.starts_with("{{") || format.starts_with("}}") {
[235](https://docs.rs#235)            out.write_str(&format[..1])
[236](https://docs.rs#236)                .map_err(|e| Error::Fmt(e, *idx))?;
[237](https://docs.rs#237)            step(2, format, idx);
[238](https://docs.rs#238)            continue;
[239](https://docs.rs#239)        }
[240](https://docs.rs#240)        if format.starts_with('{') {
[241](https://docs.rs#241)            step(1, format, idx);
[242](https://docs.rs#242)            let start = *idx;
[243](https://docs.rs#243)            let FormatArgument {
[244](https://docs.rs#244)                ident,
[245](https://docs.rs#245)                alignment,
[246](https://docs.rs#246)                sign,
[247](https://docs.rs#247)                hash,
[248](https://docs.rs#248)                zero,
[249](https://docs.rs#249)                width,
[250](https://docs.rs#250)                precision,
[251](https://docs.rs#251)                trait_,
[252](https://docs.rs#252)            } = FormatArgument::from_str(format, idx)?;
[253](https://docs.rs#253)            let value = context
[254](https://docs.rs#254)                .get(ident)
[255](https://docs.rs#255)                .ok_or(Error::MissingValue(ident.to_string(), start))?;
[256](https://docs.rs#256)            format_value(
[257](https://docs.rs#257)                out,
[258](https://docs.rs#258)                value.borrow(),
[259](https://docs.rs#259)                width,
[260](https://docs.rs#260)                precision,
[261](https://docs.rs#261)                alignment,
[262](https://docs.rs#262)                sign,
[263](https://docs.rs#263)                hash,
[264](https://docs.rs#264)                zero,
[265](https://docs.rs#265)                trait_,
[266](https://docs.rs#266)                *idx,
[267](https://docs.rs#267)                context,
[268](https://docs.rs#268)            )?;
[269](https://docs.rs#269)            ensure!(format.starts_with('}'), ParseError::Expected("}", *idx));
[270](https://docs.rs#270)            step(1, format, idx);
[271](https://docs.rs#271)            continue;
[272](https://docs.rs#272)        }
[273](https://docs.rs#273)        let next = format
[274](https://docs.rs#274)            .chars()
[275](https://docs.rs#275)            .next()
[276](https://docs.rs#276)            .expect("should contain a char if not empty");
[277](https://docs.rs#277)        out.write_char(next).map_err(|e| Error::Fmt(e, *idx))?;
[278](https://docs.rs#278)        step(next.len_utf8(), format, idx);
[279](https://docs.rs#279)    }
[280](https://docs.rs#280)    Ok(())
[281](https://docs.rs#281)}

`pub struct Formattable<'a> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Utility struct holding references to the trait implementation of a value to enable runtime verification and execution of them

# format in interpolator - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/interpolator/latest/target-redirect/i686-pc-windows-msvc/interpolator/fn.format.html

## Expand description

Runtime version of [ format!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/macro.format.html).

Takes a string and a context, containing [ Formattable](https://docs.rs/struct.Formattable.html) values, returns a
string.

```
use interpolator::{format, Formattable};
let formatted = format(
    "{value:+05}", // could be dynamic
    &[("value", Formattable::display(&12))]
        .into_iter()
        .collect::<HashMap<_, _>>(),
)
.unwrap();
assert_eq!(formatted, format!("{:+05}", 12));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

It will return an error if the specified format string has invalid syntax, the type doesn’t implement the expected trait, or the formatting itself failed.

For more details have a look at [ Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html) and

[.](https://docs.rs/enum.ParseError.html)

`ParseError`

---

# write in interpolator - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/interpolator/latest/target-redirect/i686-pc-windows-msvc/interpolator/fn.write.html

## Expand description

Runtime version of [ write!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/macro.write.html).

Takes a mutable [ Write](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/fmt/trait.Write.html) e.g.

`&mut String`, a format string and a context,
containing [values.](https://docs.rs/struct.Formattable.html)

`Formattable````
use interpolator::{write, Formattable};
let mut buf = String::new();
write(
    &mut buf,
    "{value:+05}", // could be dynamic
    &[("value", Formattable::display(&12))]
        .into_iter()
        .collect::<HashMap<_, _>>(),
)
.unwrap();
assert_eq!(buf, format!("{:+05}", 12));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

It will return an error if the specified format string has invalid syntax, the type doesn’t implement the expected trait, or the formatting itself failed.

For more details have a look at [ Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html) and

[.](https://docs.rs/enum.ParseError.html)

`ParseError`

# list in interpolator - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/interpolator/latest/target-redirect/i686-pc-windows-msvc/interpolator/macro.list.html

```
macro_rules! list {
    ($($(: $($trait:tt)?)*;)?($values:expr), *) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Creates a list of formattable values, applying th specified traits, or display if without a trait specifier.

```
use interpolator::{iformat, list};
// a list implementing Display
let list = list![: ;"test", 10, "another"];
let list = list![;"test", 10, "another"];
let list = list!["test", 10, "another"];
assert_eq!(
    iformat!("{list:i({})(, )}", list:i).unwrap(),
    "test, 10, another"
);
// a list implementing Display, Debug and UpperHex
let list = list![: :?:X; 4, 0x10, 0xa4];
assert_eq!(
    iformat!("{list:i({} {:?} {:X})(, )}", list:i).unwrap(),
    "4 4 4, 16 16 10, 164 164 A4"
);
```
Due to borrow rules you might need to create let bindings for the items, i.e.

```
let test = String::from("test");
let list = list![test];
```
instead of

# iwriteln in interpolator - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/interpolator/latest/target-redirect/i686-pc-windows-msvc/interpolator/macro.iwriteln.html

# Macro iwriteln

[Source](../src/interpolator/macros.rs.html#59-67) ```
macro_rules! iwriteln {
    ($buf: expr, $($fmt:tt)*) => { ... };
}
```

## Expand description

Like `writeln!``write()`

For details on the context syntax see `context!`

```
use std::fmt::Write;
use interpolator::iwriteln;
let mut buf = String::new();
iwriteln!(&mut buf, "{a}, {b:?}", a = 10, b:? = "test").unwrap();
assert_eq!( buf, "10, \"test\"\n" );
```

# interpolator - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/interpolator/0.5.0/i686-unknown-linux-gnu/interpolator/

## Expand description

Runtime implementation of [ format!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/macro.format.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#stdfmt-compatible-formatting)`std::fmt` compatible formatting

All options but the fill character for alignment is supported
(due to [rust-lang/rfcs#3394](https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/pull/3394)).

Though the non [ Display](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/fmt/trait.Display.html) traits need to be enabled through

[features](https://docs.rs#features).

```
use interpolator::{format, Formattable};
let formatted = format(
    "{value:+05}", // could be dynamic
    &[("value", Formattable::display(&12))]
        .into_iter()
        .collect::<HashMap<_, _>>(),
)?;
assert_eq!(formatted, format!("{:+05}", 12));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#i-iter-format)`i` iter format

The feature `iter` enables an additional format trait `i`, it allows to
format a list of values with a format string and an optional join
expression.

The syntax is `{list:i(the format string, '{}' is the array element)(the join)}`, an empty join can also be omitted `{list:i({})}`. If join is omitted
the format string `{}` can be omitted as well `{list:i}`.

Should you need to use `)` inside your format string or join, you can add `#`
similar to rust’s [raw string](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/tokens.html#raw-string-literals)
(i.e. `#(({}))#`).

It is also possible to only iterate a sub-slice specified through a range
before the format string, i.e. `{list:i1..4}`. For open ranges range
bounds can also be omitted. To index from the end, you can use negative
range bounds.

It is also possible to index a single value by only specifying an `isize``{list:i1}`.

A [ Formattable](https://docs.rs/struct.Formattable.html) implementing iter is created using

[:](https://docs.rs/struct.Formattable.html#method.iter)

`Formattable::iter````
// HashMap macro
use collection_literals::hash;
use interpolator::{format, Formattable};
// Needs to be a slice of references because `Formattable::display` expects a
// reference
let items = [&"hello", &"hi", &"hey"].map(Formattable::display);
let items = Formattable::iter(&items);
let format_str = "Greetings: {items:i..-1(`{}{outside}`)(, )} and `{items:i-1}{outside}`";
assert_eq!(
    format(format_str, &hash!("items" => items, "outside" => Formattable::display(&'!')))?,
    "Greetings: `hello!`, `hi!` and `hey!`"
);
```
See [ format()](https://docs.rs/fn.format.html) and

[for details.](https://docs.rs/fn.write.html)

`write()`[§](https://docs.rs#macros)Macros

To simplify creating contexts, some macros are provided.

- `context!`- `HashMap<&str, Formattable>`- `format()`
- `list!`- `Formattable`- [iter](https://docs.rs/%60i%60-iter-format).
- `iformat!`- `iwrite!`- `format()`- `write()`
- Most of std’s formatting macros are supported with an `i`prefix:

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

By default only [ Display](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/fmt/trait.Display.html) is supported, the rest of the

[formatting traits](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/fmt/index.html#formatting-traits)can be enabled through the following features.

- `debug`enables- `?`,- `x?`and- `X?`trait specifiers
- `number`enables- `x`,- `X`,- `b`,- `o`,- `e`and- `E`trait specifiers
- `pointer`enables- `p`trait specifiers
- `iter`enables- `i`

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros-1)

- [context](https://docs.rs/macro.context.html)
- Creates a context for use with this crate’s `format()``write()`
- [ieprint](https://docs.rs/macro.ieprint.html)
- `eprint!`- `iformat!`
- [ieprintln](https://docs.rs/macro.ieprintln.html)
- `eprintln!`- `iformat!`
- [iformat](https://docs.rs/macro.iformat.html)
- `format()`
- [iprint](https://docs.rs/macro.iprint.html)
- `print!`- `iformat!`
- [iprintln](https://docs.rs/macro.iprintln.html)
- `println!`- `iformat!`
- [iwrite](https://docs.rs/macro.iwrite.html)
- `write()`
- [iwriteln](https://docs.rs/macro.iwriteln.html)
- Like `writeln!``write()`
- [list](https://docs.rs/macro.list.html)
- Creates a list of formattable values, applying th specified traits, or display if without a trait specifier.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Formattable](https://docs.rs/struct.Formattable.html)
- Utility struct holding references to the trait implementation of a value to enable runtime verification and execution of them

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html)
- Error returned by `format()`
- [Parse](https://docs.rs/enum.ParseError.html)- Error
- Error caused by invalid format string
- [Trait](https://docs.rs/enum.Trait.html)
- The trait used to format.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Context](https://docs.rs/trait.Context.html)
- Context for `format`and`write`

[93](https://docs.rs#93)//! [formatting traits](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/fmt/index.html#formatting-traits)

[130](https://docs.rs#130)type Result<T = (), E = Error> = std::result::Result<T, E>;
[131](https://docs.rs#131)
[132](https://docs.rs#132)/// Runtime version of [`format!`].
[133](https://docs.rs#133)///
[134](https://docs.rs#134)/// Takes a string and a context, containing [`Formattable`] values, returns a
[135](https://docs.rs#135)/// string.
[136](https://docs.rs#136)///
[137](https://docs.rs#137)/// ```
[138](https://docs.rs#138)/// # use std::collections::HashMap;
[139](https://docs.rs#139)/// use interpolator::{format, Formattable};
[140](https://docs.rs#140)///
[141](https://docs.rs#141)/// let formatted = format(
[142](https://docs.rs#142)///     "{value:+05}", // could be dynamic
[143](https://docs.rs#143)///     &[("value", Formattable::display(&12))]
[144](https://docs.rs#144)///         .into_iter()
[145](https://docs.rs#145)///         .collect::<HashMap<_, _>>(),
[146](https://docs.rs#146)/// )
[147](https://docs.rs#147)/// .unwrap();
[148](https://docs.rs#148)///
[149](https://docs.rs#149)/// assert_eq!(formatted, format!("{:+05}", 12));
[150](https://docs.rs#150)/// ```
[151](https://docs.rs#151)///
[152](https://docs.rs#152)/// # Errors
[153](https://docs.rs#153)///
[154](https://docs.rs#154)/// It will return an error if the specified format string has invalid syntax,
[155](https://docs.rs#155)/// the type doesn't implement the expected trait, or the formatting itself
[156](https://docs.rs#156)/// failed.
[157](https://docs.rs#157)///
[158](https://docs.rs#158)/// For more details have a look at [`Error`] and [`ParseError`].
[159](https://docs.rs#159)pub fn format(format: &str, context: &impl Context) -> Result<String> {
[160](https://docs.rs#160)    let mut out = String::with_capacity(format.len());
[161](https://docs.rs#161)    write(&mut out, format, context)?;
[162](https://docs.rs#162)    Ok(out)
[163](https://docs.rs#163)}
[164](https://docs.rs#164)
[165](https://docs.rs#165)/// Context for `format` and `write`
[166](https://docs.rs#166)pub trait Context {
[167](https://docs.rs#167)    /// Returns the [`Formattable`] for the requested key
[168](https://docs.rs#168)    fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Option<Formattable>;
[169](https://docs.rs#169)}
[170](https://docs.rs#170)
[171](https://docs.rs#171)impl<K: Borrow<str> + Eq + Hash> Context for HashMap<K, Formattable<'_>> {
[172](https://docs.rs#172)    fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Option<Formattable> {
[173](https://docs.rs#173)        HashMap::get(self, key).copied()
[174](https://docs.rs#174)    }
[175](https://docs.rs#175)}

[177](https://docs.rs#177)#[cfg(feature = "iter")]
[178](https://docs.rs#178)struct IterContext<'a> {
[179](https://docs.rs#179)    outer: &'a dyn Context,
[180](https://docs.rs#180)    inner: Formattable<'a>,
[181](https://docs.rs#181)}
[182](https://docs.rs#182)
[183](https://docs.rs#183)#[cfg(feature = "iter")]
[184](https://docs.rs#184)impl<'a> IterContext<'a> {
[185](https://docs.rs#185)    fn new(outer: &'a impl Context, inner: Formattable<'a>) -> Self {
[186](https://docs.rs#186)        Self { outer, inner }
[187](https://docs.rs#187)    }
[188](https://docs.rs#188)}
[189](https://docs.rs#189)
[190](https://docs.rs#190)#[cfg(feature = "iter")]
[191](https://docs.rs#191)impl<'a> Context for IterContext<'a> {
[192](https://docs.rs#192)    fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Option<Formattable> {
[193](https://docs.rs#193)        if key.is_empty() {
[194](https://docs.rs#194)            Some(self.inner)
[195](https://docs.rs#195)        } else {
[196](https://docs.rs#196)            self.outer.get(key)
[197](https://docs.rs#197)        }
[198](https://docs.rs#198)    }
[199](https://docs.rs#199)}
[200](https://docs.rs#200)
[201](https://docs.rs#201)/// Runtime version of [`write!`].
[202](https://docs.rs#202)///
[203](https://docs.rs#203)/// Takes a mutable [`Write`] e.g. `&mut String`, a format string and a context,
[204](https://docs.rs#204)/// containing [`Formattable`] values.
[205](https://docs.rs#205)///
[206](https://docs.rs#206)/// ```
[207](https://docs.rs#207)/// # use std::collections::HashMap;
[208](https://docs.rs#208)/// use interpolator::{write, Formattable};
[209](https://docs.rs#209)///
[210](https://docs.rs#210)/// let mut buf = String::new();
[211](https://docs.rs#211)/// write(
[212](https://docs.rs#212)///     &mut buf,
[213](https://docs.rs#213)///     "{value:+05}", // could be dynamic
[214](https://docs.rs#214)///     &[("value", Formattable::display(&12))]
[215](https://docs.rs#215)///         .into_iter()
[216](https://docs.rs#216)///         .collect::<HashMap<_, _>>(),
[217](https://docs.rs#217)/// )
[218](https://docs.rs#218)/// .unwrap();
[219](https://docs.rs#219)///
[220](https://docs.rs#220)/// assert_eq!(buf, format!("{:+05}", 12));
[221](https://docs.rs#221)/// ```
[222](https://docs.rs#222)///
[223](https://docs.rs#223)/// # Errors
[224](https://docs.rs#224)///
[225](https://docs.rs#225)/// It will return an error if the specified format string has invalid syntax,
[226](https://docs.rs#226)/// the type doesn't implement the expected trait, or the formatting itself
[227](https://docs.rs#227)/// failed.
[228](https://docs.rs#228)///
[229](https://docs.rs#229)/// For more details have a look at [`Error`] and [`ParseError`].
[230](https://docs.rs#230)pub fn write(out: &mut impl Write, mut format: &str, context: &impl Context) -> Result {
[231](https://docs.rs#231)    let format = &mut format;
[232](https://docs.rs#232)    let idx = &mut 0;
[233](https://docs.rs#233)    while !format.is_empty() {
[234](https://docs.rs#234)        if format.starts_with("{{") || format.starts_with("}}") {
[235](https://docs.rs#235)            out.write_str(&format[..1])
[236](https://docs.rs#236)                .map_err(|e| Error::Fmt(e, *idx))?;
[237](https://docs.rs#237)            step(2, format, idx);
[238](https://docs.rs#238)            continue;
[239](https://docs.rs#239)        }
[240](https://docs.rs#240)        if format.starts_with('{') {
[241](https://docs.rs#241)            step(1, format, idx);
[242](https://docs.rs#242)            let start = *idx;
[243](https://docs.rs#243)            let FormatArgument {
[244](https://docs.rs#244)                ident,
[245](https://docs.rs#245)                alignment,
[246](https://docs.rs#246)                sign,
[247](https://docs.rs#247)                hash,
[248](https://docs.rs#248)                zero,
[249](https://docs.rs#249)                width,
[250](https://docs.rs#250)                precision,
[251](https://docs.rs#251)                trait_,
[252](https://docs.rs#252)            } = FormatArgument::from_str(format, idx)?;
[253](https://docs.rs#253)            let value = context
[254](https://docs.rs#254)                .get(ident)
[255](https://docs.rs#255)                .ok_or(Error::MissingValue(ident.to_string(), start))?;
[256](https://docs.rs#256)            format_value(
[257](https://docs.rs#257)                out,
[258](https://docs.rs#258)                value.borrow(),
[259](https://docs.rs#259)                width,
[260](https://docs.rs#260)                precision,
[261](https://docs.rs#261)                alignment,
[262](https://docs.rs#262)                sign,
[263](https://docs.rs#263)                hash,
[264](https://docs.rs#264)                zero,
[265](https://docs.rs#265)                trait_,
[266](https://docs.rs#266)                *idx,
[267](https://docs.rs#267)                context,
[268](https://docs.rs#268)            )?;
[269](https://docs.rs#269)            ensure!(format.starts_with('}'), ParseError::Expected("}", *idx));
[270](https://docs.rs#270)            step(1, format, idx);
[271](https://docs.rs#271)            continue;
[272](https://docs.rs#272)        }
[273](https://docs.rs#273)        let next = format
[274](https://docs.rs#274)            .chars()
[275](https://docs.rs#275)            .next()
[276](https://docs.rs#276)            .expect("should contain a char if not empty");
[277](https://docs.rs#277)        out.write_char(next).map_err(|e| Error::Fmt(e, *idx))?;
[278](https://docs.rs#278)        step(next.len_utf8(), format, idx);
[279](https://docs.rs#279)    }
[280](https://docs.rs#280)    Ok(())
[281](https://docs.rs#281)}

# format in interpolator - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/interpolator/latest/target-redirect/i686-unknown-linux-gnu/interpolator/fn.format.html

## Expand description

Runtime version of [ format!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/macro.format.html).

Takes a string and a context, containing [ Formattable](https://docs.rs/struct.Formattable.html) values, returns a
string.

```
use interpolator::{format, Formattable};
let formatted = format(
    "{value:+05}", // could be dynamic
    &[("value", Formattable::display(&12))]
        .into_iter()
        .collect::<HashMap<_, _>>(),
)
.unwrap();
assert_eq!(formatted, format!("{:+05}", 12));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

It will return an error if the specified format string has invalid syntax, the type doesn’t implement the expected trait, or the formatting itself failed.

For more details have a look at [ Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html) and

[.](https://docs.rs/enum.ParseError.html)

`ParseError`

# interpolator - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/interpolator/latest/target-redirect/i686-unknown-linux-gnu/interpolator/%60i%60-iter-format

## Expand description

Runtime implementation of [ format!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/macro.format.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#stdfmt-compatible-formatting)`std::fmt` compatible formatting

All options but the fill character for alignment is supported
(due to [rust-lang/rfcs#3394](https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/pull/3394)).

Though the non [ Display](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/fmt/trait.Display.html) traits need to be enabled through

[features](https://docs.rs#features).

```
use interpolator::{format, Formattable};
let formatted = format(
    "{value:+05}", // could be dynamic
    &[("value", Formattable::display(&12))]
        .into_iter()
        .collect::<HashMap<_, _>>(),
)?;
assert_eq!(formatted, format!("{:+05}", 12));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#i-iter-format)`i` iter format

The feature `iter` enables an additional format trait `i`, it allows to
format a list of values with a format string and an optional join
expression.

The syntax is `{list:i(the format string, '{}' is the array element)(the join)}`, an empty join can also be omitted `{list:i({})}`. If join is omitted
the format string `{}` can be omitted as well `{list:i}`.

Should you need to use `)` inside your format string or join, you can add `#`
similar to rust’s [raw string](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/tokens.html#raw-string-literals)
(i.e. `#(({}))#`).

It is also possible to only iterate a sub-slice specified through a range
before the format string, i.e. `{list:i1..4}`. For open ranges range
bounds can also be omitted. To index from the end, you can use negative
range bounds.

It is also possible to index a single value by only specifying an `isize``{list:i1}`.

A [ Formattable](https://docs.rs/struct.Formattable.html) implementing iter is created using

[:](https://docs.rs/struct.Formattable.html#method.iter)

`Formattable::iter````
// HashMap macro
use collection_literals::hash;
use interpolator::{format, Formattable};
// Needs to be a slice of references because `Formattable::display` expects a
// reference
let items = [&"hello", &"hi", &"hey"].map(Formattable::display);
let items = Formattable::iter(&items);
let format_str = "Greetings: {items:i..-1(`{}{outside}`)(, )} and `{items:i-1}{outside}`";
assert_eq!(
    format(format_str, &hash!("items" => items, "outside" => Formattable::display(&'!')))?,
    "Greetings: `hello!`, `hi!` and `hey!`"
);
```
See [ format()](https://docs.rs/fn.format.html) and

[for details.](https://docs.rs/fn.write.html)

`write()`[§](https://docs.rs#macros)Macros

To simplify creating contexts, some macros are provided.

- `context!`- `HashMap<&str, Formattable>`- `format()`
- `list!`- `Formattable`- [iter](https://docs.rs/%60i%60-iter-format).
- `iformat!`- `iwrite!`- `format()`- `write()`
- Most of std’s formatting macros are supported with an `i`prefix:

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

By default only [ Display](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/fmt/trait.Display.html) is supported, the rest of the

[formatting traits](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/fmt/index.html#formatting-traits)can be enabled through the following features.

- `debug`enables- `?`,- `x?`and- `X?`trait specifiers
- `number`enables- `x`,- `X`,- `b`,- `o`,- `e`and- `E`trait specifiers
- `pointer`enables- `p`trait specifiers
- `iter`enables- `i`

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros-1)

- [context](https://docs.rs/macro.context.html)
- Creates a context for use with this crate’s `format()``write()`
- [ieprint](https://docs.rs/macro.ieprint.html)
- `eprint!`- `iformat!`
- [ieprintln](https://docs.rs/macro.ieprintln.html)
- `eprintln!`- `iformat!`
- [iformat](https://docs.rs/macro.iformat.html)
- `format()`
- [iprint](https://docs.rs/macro.iprint.html)
- `print!`- `iformat!`
- [iprintln](https://docs.rs/macro.iprintln.html)
- `println!`- `iformat!`
- [iwrite](https://docs.rs/macro.iwrite.html)
- `write()`
- [iwriteln](https://docs.rs/macro.iwriteln.html)
- Like `writeln!``write()`
- [list](https://docs.rs/macro.list.html)
- Creates a list of formattable values, applying th specified traits, or display if without a trait specifier.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Formattable](https://docs.rs/struct.Formattable.html)
- Utility struct holding references to the trait implementation of a value to enable runtime verification and execution of them

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html)
- Error returned by `format()`
- [Parse](https://docs.rs/enum.ParseError.html)- Error
- Error caused by invalid format string
- [Trait](https://docs.rs/enum.Trait.html)
- The trait used to format.

# iwriteln in interpolator - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/interpolator/latest/target-redirect/i686-unknown-linux-gnu/interpolator/macro.iwriteln.html

# Macro iwriteln

[Source](../src/interpolator/macros.rs.html#59-67) ```
macro_rules! iwriteln {
    ($buf: expr, $($fmt:tt)*) => { ... };
}
```

## Expand description

Like `writeln!``write()`

For details on the context syntax see `context!`

```
use std::fmt::Write;
use interpolator::iwriteln;
let mut buf = String::new();
iwriteln!(&mut buf, "{a}, {b:?}", a = 10, b:? = "test").unwrap();
assert_eq!( buf, "10, \"test\"\n" );
```

## This enum is marked as non-exhaustive

Non-exhaustive enums could have additional variants added in future. Therefore, when matching against variants of non-exhaustive enums, an extra wildcard arm must be added to account for any future variants.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.MissingTraitImpl)

- `.0`the trait
- `.1`the byte index of the format argument

- `.1`the byte index of the format argument

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.UnsupportedOption)

- `.0`is the option
- `.1`the feature that needs to be enabled to use it
- `.2`the byte index of the format argument

### InvalidWidth([ParseIntError](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/num/error/struct.ParseIntError.html), [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html))

Unable to parse specified width as usize

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.InvalidPrecision)

### InvalidPrecision([ParseIntError](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/num/error/struct.ParseIntError.html), [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html))

Unable to parse specified precision as usize

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Fill)

### Fill([usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html))

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Iter)

### Iter([usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html))

Width, precision, `-`, `+` and `#` are not supported for `i`

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.RangeBound)

### RangeBound([ParseIntError](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/num/error/struct.ParseIntError.html), [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html))

Unable to parse specified range bound as isize

# interpolator - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/interpolator/0.5.0/x86_64-apple-darwin/interpolator/

## Expand description

Runtime implementation of [ format!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/macro.format.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#stdfmt-compatible-formatting)`std::fmt` compatible formatting

All options but the fill character for alignment is supported
(due to [rust-lang/rfcs#3394](https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/pull/3394)).

Though the non [ Display](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/fmt/trait.Display.html) traits need to be enabled through

[features](https://docs.rs#features).

```
use interpolator::{format, Formattable};
let formatted = format(
    "{value:+05}", // could be dynamic
    &[("value", Formattable::display(&12))]
        .into_iter()
        .collect::<HashMap<_, _>>(),
)?;
assert_eq!(formatted, format!("{:+05}", 12));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#i-iter-format)`i` iter format

The feature `iter` enables an additional format trait `i`, it allows to
format a list of values with a format string and an optional join
expression.

The syntax is `{list:i(the format string, '{}' is the array element)(the join)}`, an empty join can also be omitted `{list:i({})}`. If join is omitted
the format string `{}` can be omitted as well `{list:i}`.

Should you need to use `)` inside your format string or join, you can add `#`
similar to rust’s [raw string](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/tokens.html#raw-string-literals)
(i.e. `#(({}))#`).

It is also possible to only iterate a sub-slice specified through a range
before the format string, i.e. `{list:i1..4}`. For open ranges range
bounds can also be omitted. To index from the end, you can use negative
range bounds.

It is also possible to index a single value by only specifying an `isize``{list:i1}`.

A [ Formattable](https://docs.rs/struct.Formattable.html) implementing iter is created using

[:](https://docs.rs/struct.Formattable.html#method.iter)

`Formattable::iter````
// HashMap macro
use collection_literals::hash;
use interpolator::{format, Formattable};
// Needs to be a slice of references because `Formattable::display` expects a
// reference
let items = [&"hello", &"hi", &"hey"].map(Formattable::display);
let items = Formattable::iter(&items);
let format_str = "Greetings: {items:i..-1(`{}{outside}`)(, )} and `{items:i-1}{outside}`";
assert_eq!(
    format(format_str, &hash!("items" => items, "outside" => Formattable::display(&'!')))?,
    "Greetings: `hello!`, `hi!` and `hey!`"
);
```
See [ format()](https://docs.rs/fn.format.html) and

[for details.](https://docs.rs/fn.write.html)

`write()`[§](https://docs.rs#macros)Macros

To simplify creating contexts, some macros are provided.

- `context!`- `HashMap<&str, Formattable>`- `format()`
- `list!`- `Formattable`- [iter](https://docs.rs/%60i%60-iter-format).
- `iformat!`- `iwrite!`- `format()`- `write()`
- Most of std’s formatting macros are supported with an `i`prefix:

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

By default only [ Display](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/fmt/trait.Display.html) is supported, the rest of the

[formatting traits](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/fmt/index.html#formatting-traits)can be enabled through the following features.

- `debug`enables- `?`,- `x?`and- `X?`trait specifiers
- `number`enables- `x`,- `X`,- `b`,- `o`,- `e`and- `E`trait specifiers
- `pointer`enables- `p`trait specifiers
- `iter`enables- `i`

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros-1)

- [context](https://docs.rs/macro.context.html)
- Creates a context for use with this crate’s `format()``write()`
- [ieprint](https://docs.rs/macro.ieprint.html)
- `eprint!`- `iformat!`
- [ieprintln](https://docs.rs/macro.ieprintln.html)
- `eprintln!`- `iformat!`
- [iformat](https://docs.rs/macro.iformat.html)
- `format()`
- [iprint](https://docs.rs/macro.iprint.html)
- `print!`- `iformat!`
- [iprintln](https://docs.rs/macro.iprintln.html)
- `println!`- `iformat!`
- [iwrite](https://docs.rs/macro.iwrite.html)
- `write()`
- [iwriteln](https://docs.rs/macro.iwriteln.html)
- Like `writeln!``write()`
- [list](https://docs.rs/macro.list.html)
- Creates a list of formattable values, applying th specified traits, or display if without a trait specifier.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Formattable](https://docs.rs/struct.Formattable.html)
- Utility struct holding references to the trait implementation of a value to enable runtime verification and execution of them

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html)
- Error returned by `format()`
- [Parse](https://docs.rs/enum.ParseError.html)- Error
- Error caused by invalid format string
- [Trait](https://docs.rs/enum.Trait.html)
- The trait used to format.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Context](https://docs.rs/trait.Context.html)
- Context for `format`and`write`

# format in interpolator - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/interpolator/latest/target-redirect/x86_64-apple-darwin/interpolator/fn.format.html

## Expand description

Runtime version of [ format!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/macro.format.html).

Takes a string and a context, containing [ Formattable](https://docs.rs/struct.Formattable.html) values, returns a
string.

```
use interpolator::{format, Formattable};
let formatted = format(
    "{value:+05}", // could be dynamic
    &[("value", Formattable::display(&12))]
        .into_iter()
        .collect::<HashMap<_, _>>(),
)
.unwrap();
assert_eq!(formatted, format!("{:+05}", 12));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

It will return an error if the specified format string has invalid syntax, the type doesn’t implement the expected trait, or the formatting itself failed.

For more details have a look at [ Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html) and

[.](https://docs.rs/enum.ParseError.html)

`ParseError`
